## Pull request overview

Fixes schema-driven list toolbar action buttons in `apps/console` by ensuring `SchemaRenderer`-rendered `action:bar` components have an `ActionProvider` ancestor, matching the established `RecordDetailView` pattern.

**Changes:**
- Wraps `ObjectView`’s rendered tree in `ActionProvider` and wires confirm/toast/navigation/param-collection handlers.
- Adds `ListToolbarActions.test.tsx` integration tests to validate confirm-driven execution for list toolbar actions.
- Documents the fix in `CHANGELOG.md`.

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 3 out of 3 changed files in this pull request and generated 5 comments.

| File | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| apps/console/src/components/ObjectView.tsx | Introduces `ActionProvider` + handler plumbing and mounts confirm/param dialogs so toolbar actions can execute. |
| apps/console/src/__tests__/ListToolbarActions.test.tsx | Adds integration coverage for list toolbar action rendering + confirm accept/cancel behavior. |
| CHANGELOG.md | Notes the console list toolbar action wiring fix and associated tests. |

`shouldRefresh` defaults to true when `refreshAfter` is undefined (`refreshAfter !== false`). This changes the semantics from the core ActionRunner, where refresh/reload only happens when `refreshAfter === true` (see ActionRunner’s post-execution handling). Consider aligning list actions to the same contract so actions that don’t opt into refresh don’t trigger an unnecessary list refresh.

The test file header comment claims coverage for param collection dialogs and toast notifications, but the tests below only cover rendering + confirm accept/cancel (no param dialog or toast assertions). Update the comment to match what’s actually tested, or add the missing tests so the header stays accurate.
```suggestion
 * - Confirmed actions execute through the ActionProvider
 */
```

The cancel test uses a fixed `setTimeout(100)` delay before asserting `execute` wasn’t called. Fixed sleeps can make tests flaky (too short on slow CI, wasted time on fast runs). Prefer `waitFor` (or asserting immediately if cancellation is synchronous) to make the test deterministic.
